root_cause.text: The `ipc_idr_alloc()` function passed an open-ended upper bound (0) to `idr_alloc()` when allocating via the checkpoint/restore path (`ids->next_id`), allowing IDR indices to be assigned beyond `ipc_mni`, which corrupted the IDR state and led to a use-after-free during later lookups.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the upper bound from `0` to `ipc_mni` in the `idr_alloc()` call at `ipc/util.c:256` (previously `0`, now `ipc_mni`). The commit description explicitly states: "The zero upper bound makes the allocation effectively open-ended. Once the valid SysV IPC tail is occupied, idr_alloc() can spill past ipc_mni..." and "Prevent this by bounding the requested allocation to ipc_mni".

intent_record.intent_summary: Fixed a bug where the end parameter of idr_alloc was incorrectly set to 0, preventing successful IPC object allocation; changed to ipc_mni to define a valid ID range.
intent_record.what: In ipc_idr_alloc, changed the end argument of idr_alloc from 0 to ipc_mni in the else branch.
intent_record.how: The original idr_alloc call used end=0, which creates an invalid range (start >= end) causing allocation to always fail. With ipc_mni, the range becomes [start, ipc_mni), allowing proper ID allocation up to the maximum IPC index.
